# idpdbg command reference

Every operation runs as `idpdbg <group> <operation> [--param value ...]` and as the MCP tool `<group>_<operation>`, with the same parameters (`--client-id` on the command line is `client_id` over MCP). Each prints a JSON result with a `checks` list of findings (`pass`, `fail`, `warn`, `info`). Exit status: 0 ok, 1 error, 2 when a check failed.

## Common parameters

Every operation also takes these.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--profile` | string | Named profile from ~/.config/idpdbg/config.json supplying defaults (or env IDPDBG_PROFILE). |
| `--trace` | bool | Include every HTTP request and response in the result (secrets in requests are redacted). |
| `--insecure` | bool | Skip TLS certificate verification. |
| `--ca-cert` | string | Also trust these CA certificates (PEM or base64 DER), e.g. an internal or Active Directory CA: inline, or a path from the CLI or a profile. May be a file path (CLI or profile only). |
| `--timeout` | int | Per-request network timeout in seconds. Default `30`. |
| `--allow-private-urls` | bool | Let URLs that certificates or servers supply (OCSP responders, CRL locations, a provider's jwks_uri and endpoints) reach loopback, private or link-local addresses. Server-supplied URLs already may when the URL you passed points at such an address. Over MCP it must be passed in the call, never taken from a profile or the environment. |

## Secrets

A secret parameter falls back to the environment variable `IDPDBG_` plus its name in capitals, so it stays out of shell history and MCP tool arguments. These are the secret parameters:

- `--client-secret` → `IDPDBG_CLIENT_SECRET`
- `--password` → `IDPDBG_PASSWORD`
- `--refresh-token` → `IDPDBG_REFRESH_TOKEN`
- `--initial-access-token` → `IDPDBG_INITIAL_ACCESS_TOKEN`
- `--registration-access-token` → `IDPDBG_REGISTRATION_ACCESS_TOKEN`
- `--secret` → `IDPDBG_SECRET`
- `--scim-token` → `IDPDBG_SCIM_TOKEN`
- `--ldap-password` → `IDPDBG_LDAP_PASSWORD`
- `--old-password` → `IDPDBG_OLD_PASSWORD`
- `--new-password` → `IDPDBG_NEW_PASSWORD`
- `--armor-password` → `IDPDBG_ARMOR_PASSWORD`
- `--piv-pin` → `IDPDBG_PIV_PIN`
- `--pin` → `IDPDBG_PIN`
- `--credential` → `IDPDBG_CREDENTIAL`
- `--management-key` → `IDPDBG_MANAGEMENT_KEY`
- `--uri` → `IDPDBG_URI`
- `--aes-key` → `IDPDBG_AES_KEY`
- `--ssf-token` → `IDPDBG_SSF_TOKEN`
- `--continue-token` → `IDPDBG_CONTINUE_TOKEN`
- `--token` → `IDPDBG_TOKEN`
- `--tx-code` → `IDPDBG_TX_CODE`
- `--hmac-key` → `IDPDBG_HMAC_KEY`
